# Cross-account access with AWS IoT rules

AWS IoT rules can be configured so that MQTT topic data in one account is routed to AWS services in another account. Cross-account rules are configured using resource-based permissions on the destination resource. A destination supports cross-account access with AWS IoT rules only if it supports resource-based permissions. Supported cross-account destinations include Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon S3, and AWS Lambda.

For supported destinations other than Amazon SQS, the rule must be defined in the same AWS Region as the other service's resource. The destination Amazon SQS queue, by contrast, does not have to be in the same AWS Region as the AWS IoT rule.

## Prerequisites

You should be familiar with AWS IoT rules, understand IAM users, roles, and resource-based permissions, and have the AWS CLI installed.

## Account A tasks

Account A owns the rule. Do these tasks using the AWS CLI configured with account A's IAM user.

Account A's IAM user needs two permissions: `iot:CreateTopicRule`, with the rule ARN as a resource, and `iam:PassRole`, with the role ARN as a resource. This user runs the `create-topic-rule` command.

Account A also creates an IAM role that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine. The role has an attached policy that allows access to account B's destination resource. For SQS, SNS, and S3, the rule action specifies a `roleArn` that grants AWS IoT permissions to the destination.

## Account B tasks

Account B owns the destination resource. Do these tasks using the AWS CLI configured with account B's IAM user.

- **Amazon SQS:** Account B runs `sqs add-permission` to grant account A `SendMessage` permission on the queue.
- **Amazon SNS:** Account B runs `sns add-permission` to grant account A `Publish` permission on the topic.
- **Amazon S3:** Account B creates a bucket policy that trusts account A's principal and attaches it using `put-bucket-policy`. For S3 cross-account access to work, the correct Block all public access settings must be in place.
- **AWS Lambda:** Account B runs `lambda add-permission` to give AWS IoT rules permission to invoke the function. Account B's IAM user must have the `lambda:AddPermission` permission. In this command:
  - The `--principal` field gives `iot.amazonaws.com` permission to call the function.
  - The `--source-arn` field restricts triggering to the specified rule, so no other rule, in the same or a different account, can activate the function.
  - The `--source-account` field restricts AWS IoT to activating the function only on behalf of account 1111-1111-1111.

If you see a "The rule could not be found" error in the Lambda console under Configuration, you can ignore it.

## Before you begin

Complete the following before any step that needs them.

- Install the AWS CLI and configure it with IAM user credentials for both Account A and Account B. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-install.html
- Have an IAM user in Account A with `iot:CreateTopicRule` and `iam:PassRole` permissions.
- For Amazon SQS: have an IAM role in Account A that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine, with a policy allowing access to Account B's SQS queue. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-create-role.html
- For Amazon SQS: have an existing Amazon SQS queue (ExampleQueue) in Account B.
- For Amazon SNS: have an IAM role in Account A that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine, with a policy allowing access to Account B's SNS topic. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-create-role.html
- For Amazon SNS: have an existing Amazon SNS topic (ExampleTopic) in Account B.
- For Amazon S3: have an IAM role in Account A that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine, with a policy allowing access to Account B's S3 bucket. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-create-role.html
- For Amazon S3: have an existing Amazon S3 bucket in Account B (the destination).
- For Amazon S3: configure the Block all public access settings on Account B's bucket to allow cross-account access. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html
- For AWS Lambda: have an existing Lambda function (example-function) in Account B.
- For AWS Lambda: have an IAM user in Account B with `lambda:AddPermission` permission.

You should also be familiar with AWS IoT rules, and understand IAM users, roles, and resource-based permissions.

## Overview

AWS IoT rules can be configured so that MQTT topic data in one account is routed to AWS services of another account. This works only when both of the following hold: the cross-account rules are configured using resource-based permissions on the destination resource, and the destination supports cross-account access with AWS IoT rules, which it does only if it supports resource-based permissions. Support for resource-based permissions is enough to make a destination a supported cross-account destination. Supported destinations include Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon S3, and AWS Lambda.

For supported destinations other than Amazon SQS, the rule must be defined in the same AWS Region as the other service's resource. The destination Amazon SQS queue does not have to be in the same AWS Region as the AWS IoT rule.

## Account A: IAM role and rule

Account A's tasks are done using the AWS CLI configured with Account A's IAM user.

Account A creates an IAM role that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine. The role has an attached policy that allows access to Account B's destination resource. For SQS, SNS, and S3, the rule action specifies a `roleArn` that grants AWS IoT permissions to the destination; this works only when the role trusts the AWS IoT rules engine and its attached policy allows access to Account B's destination resource.

Account A's IAM user then runs the `create-topic-rule` command. This works only when the user has `iot:CreateTopicRule` permission with the rule ARN as a resource, has `iam:PassRole` permission with the role ARN as a resource, and the AWS CLI is configured with Account A's IAM user.

## Account B: granting access

Account B's tasks are done using the AWS CLI configured with Account B's IAM user. Each of the following commands works only when the CLI is configured this way.

**Amazon SQS.** Account B runs `sqs add-permission` to grant Account A `SendMessage` permission on the queue.

**Amazon SNS.** Account B runs `sns add-permission` to grant Account A `Publish` permission on the topic.

**Amazon S3.** Account B creates a bucket policy that trusts Account A's principal, then attaches it using `put-bucket-policy`. The bucket policy must be attached first, and the correct Block all public access settings must be in place, for S3 cross-account access to work. Cross-account routing to the bucket works only when both of these hold.

**AWS Lambda.** Account B runs `lambda add-permission` to give AWS IoT rules permission to invoke the function. This works only when the CLI is configured with Account B's IAM user, that user has `lambda:AddPermission` permission, and the command sets all of the following fields:

- `--principal` gives `iot.amazonaws.com` permission to call the function.
- `--source-arn` restricts triggering to the specified rule, so no other rule in the same or a different account can activate the function.
- `--source-account` restricts AWS IoT to activating the function only on behalf of account 1111-1111-1111.

If a "The rule could not be found" error appears in the Lambda console under Configuration, you can ignore it.

# Cross-account access with AWS IoT rules

You can configure AWS IoT rules so that MQTT topic data in one account is routed to AWS services in another account. Cross-account rules are configured using resource-based permissions on the destination resource, so a destination supports cross-account access with AWS IoT rules only if it supports resource-based permissions. Supported cross-account destinations include Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon S3, and AWS Lambda.

For supported destinations other than Amazon SQS, the rule must be defined in the same AWS Region as the other service's resource. The destination Amazon SQS queue, by contrast, does not have to be in the same AWS Region as the AWS IoT rule.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you should be familiar with AWS IoT rules, understand IAM users, roles, and resource-based permissions, and have the AWS CLI installed.

## Account A tasks

Account A owns the AWS IoT rule. Do its tasks using the AWS CLI configured with account A's IAM user.

Account A's IAM user needs the following permissions:

- `iot:CreateTopicRule`, with the rule ARN as a resource.
- `iam:PassRole`, with the role ARN as a resource.

The IAM user then runs the `create-topic-rule` command.

Account A also creates an IAM role that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine. The role has an attached policy that allows access to account B's destination resource. For SQS, SNS, and S3, the rule action specifies a `roleArn` that grants AWS IoT permissions to the destination.

## Account B tasks

Account B owns the destination resource. Do its tasks using the AWS CLI configured with account B's IAM user.

**Amazon SQS:** Account B runs `sqs add-permission` to grant account A `SendMessage` permission on the queue.

**Amazon SNS:** Account B runs `sns add-permission` to grant account A `Publish` permission on the topic.

**Amazon S3:** Account B creates a bucket policy that trusts account A's principal and attaches it using `put-bucket-policy`. For S3 cross-account access to work, the correct Block all public access settings must be in place.

**AWS Lambda:** Account B runs `lambda add-permission` to give AWS IoT rules permission to invoke the function. Account B's IAM user must have the `lambda:AddPermission` permission. The command uses these fields:

- `--principal` gives `iot.amazonaws.com` permission to call the function.
- `--source-arn` restricts triggering to the specified rule, so no other rule in the same or a different account can activate the function.
- `--source-account` restricts AWS IoT to activating the function only on behalf of account 1111-1111-1111.

If you see a "The rule could not be found" error in the Lambda console under **Configuration**, you can ignore it.

# Configuring cross-account AWS IoT rules

## Before you begin

You need familiarity with AWS IoT rules, and an understanding of IAM users, roles, and resource-based permissions. Complete the following before any step that depends on them.

- **AWS CLI (all scenarios):** Install the AWS CLI and configure it with IAM user credentials for each account. Installation steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-install.html.
- **SQS scenario:**
  - An Account A IAM user with `iot:CreateTopicRule` and `iam:PassRole` permissions.
  - An IAM role in Account A that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine, with a policy allowing access to Account B's SQS queue. Steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-create-role.html.
  - An existing Amazon SQS queue in Account B (the destination).
- **SNS scenario:**
  - An Account A IAM user with `iot:CreateTopicRule` and `iam:PassRole` permissions.
  - An IAM role in Account A that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine, with a policy allowing access to Account B's SNS topic. Steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-create-role.html.
  - An existing Amazon SNS topic in Account B (the destination).
- **S3 scenario:**
  - An Account A IAM user with `iot:CreateTopicRule` and `iam:PassRole` permissions.
  - An IAM role in Account A that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine, with a policy allowing access to Account B's S3 bucket. Steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-create-role.html.
  - An existing Amazon S3 bucket in Account B (the destination).
  - Block all public access settings on the Account B bucket configured to permit cross-account access. Steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html.
- **Lambda scenario:**
  - An Account A IAM user with `iot:CreateTopicRule` and `iam:PassRole` permissions.
  - An existing Lambda function in Account B (the destination).
  - An Account B IAM user with `lambda:AddPermission` permission.

## Overview

You can configure AWS IoT rules so that MQTT topic data in one account is routed to AWS services in another account. This works only when two things hold: the rule is configured using resource-based permissions on the destination resource, and the destination supports resource-based permissions with AWS IoT rules. A destination that supports resource-based permissions is enough to qualify for cross-account access. Supported cross-account destinations include Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon S3, and AWS Lambda.

For supported destinations other than Amazon SQS, the rule must be defined in the same AWS Region as the other service's resource. The destination Amazon SQS queue does not have to be in the same AWS Region as the AWS IoT rule.

In the scenarios below, Account B owns the destination resource and Account A owns the rule. Account B's tasks are done using the AWS CLI configured with Account B's IAM user. Account A's tasks are done using the AWS CLI configured with Account A's IAM user.

## Account A: role and rule creation (SQS, SNS, and S3)

In Account A, create an IAM role that trusts the AWS IoT rules engine. Attach a policy to the role that allows access to Account B's destination resource. For SQS, SNS, and S3, the rule action then specifies a `roleArn` that grants AWS IoT permissions to the destination. This works only when the role trusting the rules engine exists and its attached policy allows access to Account B's resource.

Account A's IAM user then runs the `create-topic-rule` command. The command succeeds only when the user has `iot:CreateTopicRule` permission with the rule ARN as a resource, has `iam:PassRole` permission with the role ARN as a resource, and the CLI is configured with Account A's IAM user.

## Account B: granting access

**SQS.** Using the CLI configured with Account B's IAM user, Account B runs `sqs add-permission` to grant Account A `SendMessage` permission on the queue. This works only when the CLI is configured with Account B's IAM user.

**SNS.** Using the CLI configured with Account B's IAM user, Account B runs `sns add-permission` to grant Account A `Publish` permission on the topic. This also works only when the CLI is configured with Account B's IAM user.

**S3.** Account B creates a bucket policy that trusts Account A's principal, then attaches it using `put-bucket-policy`. Cross-account routing to S3 works only when the bucket policy has been attached with `put-bucket-policy` and the Block all public access settings are correctly in place. Without both, S3 cross-account access will not work.

## Lambda

For Lambda, Account B runs `lambda add-permission` to give AWS IoT rules permission to invoke the function. This works only when the CLI is configured with Account B's IAM user, that user has `lambda:AddPermission` permission, and the command sets the following three fields:

- `--principal` gives `iot.amazonaws.com` permission to call the function.
- `--source-arn` restricts triggering to the specified rule, so no other rule in the same or a different account can activate the function.
- `--source-account` restricts AWS IoT to activating the function only on behalf of account 1111-1111-1111.

If the Lambda console shows a "The rule could not be found" error under Configuration, you can ignore it.
